---
title: "Sample-path bounds"
---

## Motivation

In the previous lectures, we have obtained bounds on policy error, value error, and model approximation error in terms of the sup-norm. In this lecture, we will develop sample path based bounds which are tighter. For simplicity, we reuse some of the symbols from the previous lectures, but their meanings are different.

## Model approximation (Take 3)

### One step error propagation

Recall that the **model operator** $\MODEL_t \colon \ALPHABET V \to \ALPHABET Q$ includes both the cost and the transition:
$$
  [\MODEL_t v](s,a)
  = c_t(s,a) + \sum_{s' \in \ALPHABET S} P_t(s' \mid s,a) v(s').
$$
Define the **dynamics operator** $\DYNAMICS_t \colon \ALPHABET V \to \ALPHABET Q$ to be the transition part alone:
$$
  [\DYNAMICS_t v](s,a) 
  = \sum_{s' \in \ALPHABET S} P_t(s' \mid s,a) v(s').
$$
Thus $\MODEL_t v = c_t + \DYNAMICS_t v$. As before, the mismatch is $\MISMATCH_t v = \MODEL_t v - \hat \MODEL_t v$.

:::{#lem-model-diff}

For any $v, \hat v \in \ALPHABET V$,
$$
  \MODEL_t v - \MODEL_t \hat v
  = \DYNAMICS_t \bigl[ v - \hat v \bigr].
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

The cost terms cancel:
\begin{align*}
  \MODEL_t v - \MODEL_t \hat v
  &= \bigl(c_t + \DYNAMICS_t v\bigr)
  - \bigl(c_t + \DYNAMICS_t \hat v\bigr)
  = \DYNAMICS_t v - \DYNAMICS_t \hat v
  = \DYNAMICS_t \bigl[ v - \hat v \bigr],
\end{align*}
where the last step uses linearity of $\DYNAMICS_t$.
:::

:::{#lem-one-step-signed}
#### One step error propagation

Given $v_{t+1}, \hat v_{t+1} \in \ALPHABET V$, define $q_t = \MODEL_t v_{t+1}$ and $\hat q_t = \hat \MODEL_t \hat v_{t+1}$. Then
$$
  q_t - \hat q_t
  = \MISMATCH_t \hat v_{t+1}
  + \bigl[
    \MODEL_t v_{t+1} - \MODEL_t \hat v_{t+1}
  \bigr]
  = \MISMATCH_t \hat v_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t \bigl[ v_{t+1} - \hat v_{t+1} \bigr].
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

Consider
\begin{align*}
  q_t - \hat q_t
  &= \MODEL_t v_{t+1} - \hat \MODEL_t \hat v_{t+1}
  \\
  &= \bigl[
    \MODEL_t \hat v_{t+1} - \hat \MODEL_t \hat v_{t+1}
  \bigr]
  + \bigl[
    \MODEL_t v_{t+1} - \MODEL_t \hat v_{t+1}
  \bigr]
  \\
  &= \MISMATCH_t \hat v_{t+1}
  + \bigl[
    \MODEL_t v_{t+1} - \MODEL_t \hat v_{t+1}
  \bigr]
  \\
  &= \MISMATCH_t \hat v_{t+1}
  + \DYNAMICS_t \bigl[ v_{t+1} - \hat v_{t+1} \bigr],
\end{align*}
where the third equality uses the definition of $\MISMATCH_t$ and the last equality uses @lem-model-diff.
:::

### Policy error

:::{#prp-policy-error-signed}
#### Policy error

For any policy $π = (π_1, \dots, π_T)$, define the policy errors
$$
  α^π_t(s)
  \coloneqq V^π_t(s) - \hat V^π_t(s),
  \qquad
  β^π_t(s,a)
  \coloneqq Q^π_t(s,a) - \hat Q^π_t(s,a),
$$
with the convention $α^π_{T+1} ≡ 0$. Then, for any $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$ and all $(s,a) \in \ALPHABET S \times \ALPHABET A$,
\begin{align*}
  β^π_t
  &= Δ^π_t
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^π_{t+1},
  \\
  α^π_t(s)
  &= β^π_t\bigl(s, π_t(s)\bigr),
\end{align*}
where
$$
  Δ^π_t
  \coloneqq \MISMATCH_t \hat V^π_{t+1}.
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

Recall that
$$
  Q^π_t = \MODEL_t V^π_{t+1},
  \quad
  \hat Q^π_t = \hat \MODEL_t \hat V^π_{t+1},
$$
and $V^π_t = \ALPHABET T^{π_t} Q^π_t$, $\hat V^π_t = \ALPHABET T^{π_t} \hat Q^π_t$. From @lem-one-step-signed with $v_{t+1} = V^π_{t+1}$ and $\hat v_{t+1} = \hat V^π_{t+1}$,
$$
  β^π_t
  = Q^π_t - \hat Q^π_t
  = Δ^π_t + \DYNAMICS_t α^π_{t+1}.
$$
Evaluating at $a = π_t(s)$ and using that $π_t$ is deterministic,
$$
  α^π_t(s)
  = V^π_t(s) - \hat V^π_t(s)
  = Q^π_t\bigl(s, π_t(s)\bigr) - \hat Q^π_t\bigl(s, π_t(s)\bigr)
  = β^π_t\bigl(s, π_t(s)\bigr).
$$
:::

### Value error

Similar to the above, we can also compare the optimal value functions of the true and approximate models.

:::{#prp-value-error-signed}
#### Value error

Define the value errors
$$
  α^\star_t(s)
  \coloneqq V^\star_t(s) - \hat V^\star_t(s),
  \qquad
  β^\star_t(s,a)
  \coloneqq Q^\star_t(s,a) - \hat Q^\star_t(s,a),
$$
with the convention $α^\star_{T+1} ≡ 0$. Then, for any $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$ and all $(s,a) \in \ALPHABET S \times \ALPHABET A$,
\begin{align*}
  β^\star_t
  &= Δ^\star_t
  + \DYNAMICS_t α^\star_{t+1},
  \\
  β^\star_t\bigl(s, π^\star_t(s)\bigr)
  &\le α^\star_t(s)
  \le β^\star_t\bigl(s, \hat π^\star_t(s)\bigr),
\end{align*}
where
$$
  Δ^\star_t
  \coloneqq \MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}.
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

Recall that
$$
  Q^\star_t = \MODEL_t V^\star_{t+1},
  \quad
  \hat Q^\star_t = \hat \MODEL_t \hat V^\star_{t+1},
$$
and $V^\star_t = \ALPHABET T^\star Q^\star_t$, $\hat V^\star_t = \ALPHABET T^\star \hat Q^\star_t$. From @lem-one-step-signed with $v_{t+1} = V^\star_{t+1}$ and $\hat v_{t+1} = \hat V^\star_{t+1}$,
$$
  β^\star_t
  = Q^\star_t - \hat Q^\star_t
  = Δ^\star_t + \DYNAMICS_t α^\star_{t+1}.
$$

The sandwich for $α^\star_t$ uses the two optimality properties, one at a time.

*Upper bound.* By optimality of $\hat π^\star_t$ on the approximate side, $\hat V^\star_t(s) = \hat Q^\star_t\bigl(s, \hat π^\star_t(s)\bigr)$, while on the true side $V^\star_t(s) = \inf_{a} Q^\star_t(s,a) \le Q^\star_t\bigl(s, \hat π^\star_t(s)\bigr)$. Therefore
$$
  α^\star_t(s) = V^\star_t(s) - \hat V^\star_t(s)
  \le Q^\star_t\bigl(s, \hat π^\star_t(s)\bigr)
  - \hat Q^\star_t\bigl(s, \hat π^\star_t(s)\bigr)
  = β^\star_t\bigl(s, \hat π^\star_t(s)\bigr).
$$

*Lower bound.* By optimality of $π^\star_t$ on the true side, $V^\star_t(s) = Q^\star_t\bigl(s, π^\star_t(s)\bigr)$, while on the approximate side $\hat V^\star_t(s) = \inf_{a} \hat Q^\star_t(s,a) \le \hat Q^\star_t\bigl(s, π^\star_t(s)\bigr)$. Therefore
$$
  α^\star_t(s)
  = V^\star_t(s) - \hat V^\star_t(s)
  \ge Q^\star_t\bigl(s, π^\star_t(s)\bigr)
  - \hat Q^\star_t\bigl(s, π^\star_t(s)\bigr)
  = β^\star_t\bigl(s, π^\star_t(s)\bigr).
$$
:::

Unfortunately, the result of @thm-value-error-signed is uncomputable because we do not know the exact value of $\alpha^\star_t$. However, as we explain below, it can be used to obtain model approximation error bounds by upper and lower bounding $\alpha^\star_t$.

### Model approximation bounds

As in the sup-norm case, the key idea is that
$$
  0 \le V^{\hat \pi^\star}_t - V^\star_t
  \le \bigl[\hat V^{\hat \pi^\star}_t - V^{\hat \pi^\star}_t \bigr]
    - \bigl[ V^\star_t - \hat V^\star_t \bigr].
$$
So, we can take an upper bound on the first term and a lower bound on the second term to get a bound on the model error. We can get these (possibly loose) upper and lower bounds on $α^{\hat π^\star}$ and $α^\star$ by finding $(α^+, β^+)$ and $(α^-, β^-)$ that obey the same recursions but with inequalities instead of equalities.

:::{#thm-signed-sample-path}
#### Signed sample-path bound

Suppose that for each $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$ there exist functions $α^+_t, α^-_t \colon \ALPHABET S \to \reals$ and $β^+_t, β^-_t \colon \ALPHABET S \times \ALPHABET A \to \reals$ such that
$$
  β^-_T(s,a) \le Δ^\star_T(s,a) \le β^+_T(s,a),
$$
and for $t < T$,
\begin{align*}
  β^-_t(s,a)
  &\le Δ^\star_t(s,a)
  + \sum_{s'} α^-_{t+1}(s') P_t(s' \mid s,a),
  \\
  α^-_t(s)
  &\le β^-_t\bigl(s, π^\star_t(s)\bigr),
\end{align*}
and 
\begin{align*}
  β^+_t(s,a)
  &\ge Δ^\star_t(s,a)
  + \sum_{s'} α^+_{t+1}(s') P_t(s' \mid s,a),
  \\
  α^+_t(s)
  &\ge β^+_t\bigl(s, \hat π^\star_t(s)\bigr),
\end{align*}
where $Δ^\star_t$ is as in @prp-value-error-signed. Then, for all $t$ and $s$,
$$
  V^{\hat π^\star}_t(s) - V^\star_t(s)
  \le α^+_t(s) - α^-_t(s).
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

The recursions for the upper bound and the lower bound are similar to the recursions for exact policy and value errors in @prp-policy-error-signed (specialized to $\hat π^\star$) and @prp-value-error-signed, with equalities replaced by inequalities. Therefore, a backward induction argument shows that $α^+_t$ is an upper bound on $α^{\hat π^\star}_t = V^{\hat π^\star}_t - \hat V^\star_t$ and $α^-_t$ is a lower bound on $α^\star_t = V^\star_t - \hat V^\star_t$. Combining the two inequalities then gives
$$
  V^{\hat π^\star}_t(s) - V^\star_t(s)
  = α^{\hat π^\star}_t(s) - α^\star_t(s)
  \le α^+_t(s) - α^-_t(s).
$$
:::

A concrete construction that uses the best upper bound and relaxes the lower bound (so that we don't need the knowledge of $π^\star$) is
\begin{align*}
  α^+_t(s)
  &= Δ^\star_t\bigl(s, \hat π^\star_t(s)\bigr)
  + \sum_{s'} α^+_{t+1}(s')
  P_t\bigl(s' \mid s, \hat π^\star_t(s)\bigr),
  \\
  α^-_t(s)
  &= \min_{a \in \ALPHABET C_t(s)}
  \Bigl[
    Δ^\star_t(s,a)
    + \sum_{s'} α^-_{t+1}(s') P_t(s' \mid s,a)
  \Bigr],
\end{align*}
where $\ALPHABET C_t(s) \subseteq \ALPHABET A$ is any set guaranteed to contain $π^\star_t(s)$ (for example $\ALPHABET C_t(s) = \ALPHABET A$, or a structural candidate set that does not require computing $π^\star$ explicitly). @thm-signed-sample-path then guarantees
$$
  V^{\hat π^\star}_t(s) - V^\star_t(s)
  \le α^+_t(s) - α^-_t(s).
$$

### Symmetric bounds

The above bound requires separately keeping track of an upper and lower bound. We can get symmetric upper and lower bounds by taking absolute values.

:::{#thm-abs-sample-path}
#### Absolute-value sample-path bound

Suppose that for each $t \in \{1,\dots,T\}$ there exist functions $α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t \colon \ALPHABET S \to \reals_{\ge 0}$ and $β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t \colon \ALPHABET S \times \ALPHABET A \to \reals_{\ge 0}$ such that
$$
  β^{\mathrm{abs}}_T(s,a) \ge \ABS{Δ^\star_T(s,a)},
$$
and for $t < T$,
$$
  β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t(s,a)
  \ge \ABS{Δ^\star_t(s,a)}
  + \sum_{s' \in \ALPHABET S}
  α^{\mathrm{abs}}_{t+1}(s')
  P_t(s' \mid s,a),
$$
and for all $t$,
$$
  α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t(s)
  \ge \max\Bigl\{
    β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t\bigl(s, π^\star_t(s)\bigr),\;
    β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t\bigl(s, \hat π^\star_t(s)\bigr)
  \Bigr\},
$$
where $Δ^\star_t$ is as in @prp-value-error-signed. Then the policy $\hat π^\star$ satisfies, for all $t$ and $s$,
$$
  \ABS{V^{\hat π^\star}_t(s) - V^\star_t(s)}
  \le 2 α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t(s).
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note collapse="false"}
#### Proof

Choose the upper and lower bounds
$$
  α^+_t = α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t,
  \quad
  α^-_t = -α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t,
  \quad
  β^+_t = β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t,
  \quad
  β^-_t = -β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t.
$$
These satisfy the hypotheses of @thm-signed-sample-path, so
$$
  V^{\hat π^\star}_t(s) - V^\star_t(s)
  \le α^+_t(s) - α^-_t(s)
  = 2 α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t(s).
$$
For the matching lower side, optimality of $V^\star$ yields $V^{\hat π^\star}_t(s) - V^\star_t(s) \ge 0 \ge -2 α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t(s)$ because $α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t \ge 0$. Combining the two inequalities gives the claim.
:::

A feasible (but state-independent) choice is
$$
  α^{\mathrm{abs}}_t(s)
  \equiv \sum_{\tau=t}^{T} \NORM{\MISMATCH_\tau \hat V^\star_{\tau+1}},
  \qquad
  β^{\mathrm{abs}}_t(s,a)
  \equiv \NORM{\MISMATCH_t \hat V^\star_{t+1}}
  + \sum_{s'} α^{\mathrm{abs}}_{t+1}(s') P_t(s' \mid s,a).
$$
For this choice, @thm-abs-sample-path recovers the factor-of-two model-approximation bound from the model-approximation lecture:
$$
  \NORM{V^{\hat π^\star}_t - V^\star_t}
  \le 2 \sum_{\tau=t}^{T} \NORM{\MISMATCH_\tau \hat V^\star_{\tau+1}}.
$$

## Computing the bounds

One difficulty in applying @thm-signed-sample-path is that the upper and lower bound recursions propagate with the true kernel $P_t$. In applications where $P_t$ is unknown or inconvenient to evaluate, we can obtain coarser bounds that use only the approximate kernel $\hat P_t$, at the price of an additional IPM penalty.

Let $\def\F{\mathcal{F}}\F$ be a (maximal) generator as in the model-approximation lecture, with IPM $d_{\F}$ and Minkowski functional $ρ_{\F}$. Define the pointwise transition discrepancy
$$
  δ_t(s,a)
  \coloneqq d_{\F}\bigl(P_t(\cdot \mid s,a), \hat P_t(\cdot \mid s,a)\bigr).
$$
The defining IPM inequality then yields, for any $α \colon \ALPHABET S \to \reals$,
$$
  \ABS{
    \sum_{s'} α(s') P_t(s' \mid s,a)
    - \sum_{s'} α(s') \hat P_t(s' \mid s,a)
  }
  \le δ_t(s,a)\, ρ_{\F}(α).
$$
Equivalently,
\begin{align*}
  \sum_{s'} α(s') P_t(s' \mid s,a)
  &\le \sum_{s'} α(s') \hat P_t(s' \mid s,a)
  + δ_t(s,a)\, ρ_{\F}(α),
  \\
  \sum_{s'} α(s') P_t(s' \mid s,a)
  &\ge \sum_{s'} α(s') \hat P_t(s' \mid s,a)
  - δ_t(s,a)\, ρ_{\F}(α).
\end{align*}

Thus any average of an upper or lower bound with respect to the true dynamics can be replaced by the corresponding average with respect to the approximate dynamics plus or minus an IPM correction. In particular, the upper recursion of @thm-signed-sample-path is implied by
$$
  β^+_t(s,a)
  \ge Δ^\star_t(s,a)
  + \sum_{s'} α^+_{t+1}(s') \hat P_t(s' \mid s,a)
  + δ_t(s,a)\, ρ_{\F}(α^+_{t+1}),
$$
and the lower recursion is implied by
$$
  β^-_t(s,a)
  \le Δ^\star_t(s,a)
  + \sum_{s'} α^-_{t+1}(s') \hat P_t(s' \mid s,a)
  - δ_t(s,a)\, ρ_{\F}(α^-_{t+1}).
$$
The resulting bounds are typically looser than those built from $P_t$, but they are computable from the approximate model together with the IPM discrepancies $δ_t$.
